technical_and_design_decisions: All ported/moved modules will be implemented as standalone Spring Boot applications using the Spring Cloud Stream programming model (@EnableBinding with Source/Processor interfaces) instead of the legacy Spring XD module model.

Module configuration options will be exposed through @ConfigurationProperties classes, with metadata generated via the spring-boot-configuration-processor so the shell can enumerate and describe module properties (U2).

The shell (U1) will be built on Spring Shell and will act purely as a client of the existing spring-cloud-data REST API, using a RestTemplate-based client layer; scope is restricted to stream lifecycle commands (create, deploy, undeploy, destroy, list) plus the 'module info' command.
The http source (U3) will expose a Spring MVC endpoint in a Spring Boot app that maps incoming HTTP requests to the source output channel.
The tcp source (U4) will be built on Spring Integration TCP inbound adapters with configurable connection factories and (de)serializers/codecs ported from XD.

Twitter source modules (U5, U6) will reuse Spring Social Twitter with externalized OAuth credentials; twittersearch will reuse the common Twitter connection/configuration code established for twitterstream.
Filter (U7) and transform (U8) processors will use SpEL expressions evaluated against incoming messages, matching XD behavior.

Build is a Maven multi-module project with a shared parent POM, common test-support utilities, and per-module integration tests; JUnit/Mockito for unit tests and Spring integration test support with an embedded binder for end-to-end tests.
Target stack assumed: Java 17, Spring Boot / Spring Cloud Stream / Spring Cloud Data current release lines.
assumptions: The spring-cloud-data REST API for stream operations already exists and is stable; no server-side work is required for U1.
The legacy Spring XD module source code is available as a reference, so porting consists of adaptation to the Spring Cloud Stream binder model rather than new feature design.
Scope of U1 is limited to stream commands only, as stated; other shell commands (task, metrics, etc.) are out of scope.
U2 covers listing/displaying module properties via 'module info' only; no property validation UI or editing features are required.
Twitter developer credentials and sandbox accounts are available for development and testing of U5 and U6.
A running binder (e.g., Kafka/Rabbit) and a local spring-cloud-data server are available for integration testing.

Estimates are ideal effort for a single experienced Spring developer performing all work (design, coding, testing, documentation); code review, release management, and deployment to production are excluded.
No performance/load testing or security hardening beyond standard framework defaults is required.

activities.activity_description: Analyze the legacy XD modules and the spring-cloud-data REST API, define the porting approach, module structure, shell command design, and metadata strategy outline.
Set up the multi-module build (parent POM, module scaffolding, dependency management), common test-support utilities, and continuous integration configuration.

Design and implement the mechanism that derives module option metadata from @ConfigurationProperties classes (configuration processor integration, metadata exposure for the data server/shell), including unit and integration tests.
Implement the shell command that retrieves and renders module property metadata (names, types, defaults, descriptions) from the data server, with tests and help text.

activities.activity_name: U1: REST client for stream operations
activities.activity_description: Implement a RestTemplate-based client layer for the spring-cloud-data stream endpoints (create, deploy, undeploy, destroy, list), including model classes, error handling, and unit tests with mocked server.

Implement the Spring Shell commands for stream lifecycle (create, deploy, undeploy, destroy, list) with tabular output formatting, option parsing, integration tests against a local data server, and user documentation.
Port the XD http module to a Spring Cloud Stream source (HTTP endpoint mapped to output channel, @ConfigurationProperties options), including unit/integration tests and README.

Port the XD tcp module to a Spring Cloud Stream source using Spring Integration TCP adapters, with configurable connection factories, codecs/serializers, @ConfigurationProperties options, tests, and README.
Move the XD twitterstream module to a Spring Cloud Stream source using Spring Social Twitter, externalize OAuth configuration via @ConfigurationProperties, with tests and README.
Move the XD twittersearch module to a Spring Cloud Stream source, reusing the common Twitter connection/configuration code from A9, with tests and README.
Port the XD filter module to a Spring Cloud Stream processor using SpEL expression evaluation, with @ConfigurationProperties options, tests, and README.
Port the XD transform module to a Spring Cloud Stream processor using SpEL expression evaluation, with @ConfigurationProperties options, tests, and README.
Run end-to-end pipeline tests (source-processor-sink via the shell against a local data server and binder), finalize reference/user documentation, and prepare module packaging for release.
